Seasonal Variations¶

In [84]:
# Group by Season and Ponds to get mean values
season_group = df.groupby(["Season", "Ponds"]).mean(numeric_only=True).reset_index()
In [85]:
# Function to plot each variable
def plot_seasonal(variable, ylabel):
    plt.figure(figsize=(10,6))
    
    for pond in season_group["Ponds"].unique():
        pond_data = season_group[season_group["Ponds"] == pond]
        plt.plot(pond_data["Season"], pond_data[variable], label=pond)
    
    plt.xlabel("Season")
    plt.ylabel(ylabel)
    plt.title(f"Seasonal Variation in {ylabel} Across Ponds")
    plt.legend()
    plt.show()

# Plot Temperature
plot_seasonal("Temperature", "Water Temperature (°C)")

# Plot pH
plot_seasonal("pH", "pH")

# Plot Conductivity
plot_seasonal("Conductivity", "Conductivity (µS/cm)")

Annual Variation¶

In [87]:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import calendar
# Ensure numeric columns
for col in ["Temperature", "pH", "Conductivity"]:
    df[col] = pd.to_numeric(df[col], errors="coerce")

# Month ordering and labels
month_order = list(range(1, 13))
month_labels = [calendar.month_abbr[m] for m in month_order]

# Compute monthly climatology (mean across all years) per pond
monthly = (
    df.groupby(["Month", "Ponds"], as_index=False)
      .mean(numeric_only=True)
      .sort_values("Month")
)

# Helper to plot
def plot_monthly(variable, ylabel, outfile):
    plt.figure(figsize=(12,6))
    for pond in monthly["Ponds"].unique():
        sub = monthly[monthly["Ponds"] == pond]
        # Align by month order
        sub = sub.set_index("Month").reindex(month_order).reset_index()
        plt.plot(sub["Month"], sub[variable], label=pond)
    plt.xticks(month_order, month_labels, rotation=0)
    plt.xlabel("Month")
    plt.ylabel(ylabel)
    plt.title(f"Monthly (Jan–Dec) Variation in {ylabel} Across Inflow and Ponds")
    plt.legend(title="Site", ncol=2)
    plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.savefig(outfile, dpi=200, bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.show()

# Create three plots and save
plot_monthly("Temperature", "Water Temperature (°C)", "C:/Users/User/Desktop/Assignment_1/Nutrients_Analysis/monthly_temperature.png")
plot_monthly("pH", "pH", "C:/Users/User/Desktop/Assignment_1/Nutrients_Analysis/monthly_pH.png")
plot_monthly("Conductivity", "Conductivity (µS/cm)", "C:/Users/User/Desktop/Assignment_1/Nutrients_Analysis/monthly_conductivity.png")

# Also export the monthly means table for reference
monthly_out = monthly.copy()
monthly_out["Month_Label"] = monthly_out["Month"].map({i: calendar.month_abbr[i] for i in month_order})
monthly_out = monthly_out[["Month", "Month_Label", "Ponds", "Temperature", "pH", "Conductivity"]]
monthly_out.to_csv("C:/Users/User/Desktop/Assignment_1/Nutrients_Analysis/monthly_means_by_pond.csv", index=False)

Kruskal Wallis to show Significance Difference between the Ponds and our target Western Spring Inflow¶

In [93]:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.stats import kruskal
In [94]:
# Ensure numeric
for col in ["Temperature", "pH", "Conductivity"]:
    df[col] = pd.to_numeric(df[col], errors="coerce")

# List ponds
ponds = df["Ponds"].unique()

results = {}

for variable in ["Temperature", "pH", "Conductivity"]:
    groups = [df[df["Ponds"] == pond][variable].dropna() for pond in ponds]
    stat, p = kruskal(*groups)
    results[variable] = {"Statistic": stat, "p-value": p}

results

Scatter plots and Regression Analysis¶

In [99]:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np

#Ensure numeric
for col in ["Temperature", "pH", "Conductivity"]:
    df[col] = pd.to_numeric(df[col], errors="coerce")

# Drop missing values
df = df.dropna(subset=["Temperature", "pH", "Conductivity"])

def scatter_regression(x, y, xlabel, ylabel, filename):
    plt.figure(figsize=(8,6))
    plt.scatter(df[x], df[y])
    
    # Regression line
    m, b = np.polyfit(df[x], df[y], 1)
    x_vals = np.linspace(df[x].min(), df[x].max(), 100)
    y_vals = m * x_vals + b
    plt.plot(x_vals, y_vals)
    
    plt.xlabel(xlabel)
    plt.ylabel(ylabel)
    plt.title(f"{ylabel} vs {xlabel}")
    plt.savefig(filename, dpi=300, bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.show()

# 1) Conductivity vs Temperature
scatter_regression("Temperature", "Conductivity", "Water Temperature (°C)", "Conductivity (µS/cm)", "C:/Users/User/Desktop/Assignment_1/Nutrients_Analysis/reg_temp_cond.png")

# 2) pH vs Temperature

def scatter_regression(x, y, xlabel, ylabel, filename):
    plt.figure(figsize=(8,6))
    plt.scatter(df[x], df[y])
    
    # Regression line
    m, b = np.polyfit(df[x], df[y], 1)
    x_vals = np.linspace(df[x].min(), df[x].max(), 100)
    y_vals = m * x_vals + b
    plt.plot(x_vals, y_vals)
    
    plt.xlabel(xlabel)
    plt.ylabel(ylabel)
    plt.title(f"{ylabel} vs {xlabel}")
    plt.savefig(filename, dpi=300, bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.show()

In [104]:
# Ensure numeric
for col in ["Temperature", "pH", "Conductivity"]:
    df[col] = pd.to_numeric(df[col], errors="coerce")

df = df.dropna(subset=["Temperature", "pH", "Conductivity"])

# Function to compute correlations
def correlations(x, y):
    pear = pearsonr(df[x], df[y])
    spear = spearmanr(df[x], df[y])
    return pear, spear

corr_results = {}

pairs = [
    ("Temperature", "Conductivity"),
    ("Temperature", "pH"),
    ("pH", "Conductivity")
]

for x, y in pairs:
    pear, spear = correlations(x, y)
    corr_results[f"{y} vs {x}"] = {
        "Pearson_r": pear[0],
        "Pearson_p": pear[1],
        "Spearman_r": spear[0],
        "Spearman_p": spear[1]
    }

# Linear regression function
def regression(x, y):
    X = sm.add_constant(df[x])
    model = sm.OLS(df[y], X).fit()
    return model.summary()

reg_temp_cond = regression("Temperature", "Conductivity")
reg_temp_pH = regression("Temperature", "pH")
reg_pH_cond = regression("pH", "Conductivity")

# Function to do regression and plot
def regress_plot(x, y, xlabel, ylabel, filename):
    sub = merged[[x,y]].dropna()
    X = sm.add_constant(sub[x])
    model = sm.OLS(sub[y], X).fit()
    slope = model.params[x]
    intercept = model.params["const"]
    r2 = model.rsquared
    
    # Pearson r
    r, p = pearsonr(sub[x], sub[y])
    
    # Plot
    plt.figure(figsize=(7,5))
    plt.scatter(sub[x], sub[y], s=35, alpha=0.7)
    xs = np.linspace(sub[x].min(), sub[x].max(), 100)
    plt.plot(xs, slope*xs + intercept, linewidth=2)
    plt.xlabel(xlabel)
    plt.ylabel(ylabel)
    plt.title(f"{ylabel} vs {xlabel}\nR²={r2:.2f}, r={r:.2f}, p={p:.4f}")
    plt.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
    plt.savefig(filename, dpi=300, bbox_inches="tight")
    plt.show()
    
    return r2, r, p, slope, intercept

Perform Dunn’s post-hoc to check which ponds differ significantly¶

In [126]:
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from scipy.stats import mannwhitneyu
from statsmodels.stats.multitest import multipletests

for col in ["Temperature", "pH", "Conductivity"]:
    df[col] = pd.to_numeric(df[col], errors="coerce")

# Focus on Western Arm vs Inflow only
pairs = [("Western_Arm_Spring_Inflow", "Western_Arm")]
variables = ["Temperature", "pH", "Conductivity"]

results = []

for var in variables:
    g1 = df[df["Ponds"] == "Western_Arm_Spring_Inflow"][var].dropna()
    g2 = df[df["Ponds"] == "Western_Arm"][var].dropna()
    stat, p = mannwhitneyu(g1, g2, alternative="two-sided")
    results.append([var, stat, p])

mw_df = pd.DataFrame(results, columns=["Variable","Statistic Mann-Whitney U","p_value"])

# Holm correction
mw_df["p_value_corrected"] = multipletests(mw_df["p_value"], method="holm")[1]
mw_df

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from sklearn.inspection import PartialDependenceDisplay

# If you didn't run tuning, replace best_rf with rf
model = best_rf  # or: model = rf
In [174]:
feature = "Conductivity"  # <- change to any column in X_aligned
plt.figure(figsize=(6,4))
PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(model, X_aligned, [feature], kind="average")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
